annotations.title: The Epiſtle of Chriſt.
annotations.text: [1] S. Paul and other holy vvriters of Scriptures did ſet downe many thinges in writing, by penne, inke, and paper, al which be of the Holy Ghoſt: but the ſpecial and proper booke of Chriſtes truth and Goſpel, is not the external writing in thoſe dead creatures, but in the hartes of the faithful, being the proper ſubiecte of theſe truthes and graces preached in the nevv Teſtament, and the habitacle of the Holy Ghoſt. In the vvhich booke of faithful mens hartes S. Paul vvrote diuers thinges not vttered in any Epiſtle: as ſundrie of the Apoſtles wrote the Chriſtian religion in the hartes of their hearers onely, and in other material bookes not at all. Whereof S. Irenæus li. 3. c. 4. ſaith, [2] What and if the Apoſtles alſo had left no Scriptures, ought we not to follow the order of the tradition, which they deliuered vnto them to whom they committed the Churches? to the which ordinance many nations of thoſe barbarous people that haue beleeued in Chriſt, do conſent, vvithout letter or inke, hauing ſaluation written in their hartes, and keeping diligently the tradition of the elders. And S. Hierom, (cont. Io. Hieros. c. 9. ad Pam.) In the Creede of our faith and hope, which being deliuered by tradition from the Apoſtles, is not written in paper and inke, but in the tables carnal of the hart. And this is the Churches booke alſo, vvhereby and wherein ſhe keepeth faithfully al truth written in the hartes of thoſe to vvhom the Apoſtles did preach, vvith the like diligence as ſhe keepeth and preſerueth the other booke vvhich is of holy Scriptures, from al corruption of Heretikes and other iniuries.

notes.text: The Apostles wrote the Gospel in mens hartes much more then in paper.

annotations.title: Of our ſelues.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> This maketh firſt againſt the Heretikes called Pelagians, that hold our meritorious actions or cogitations to be of free vvil onely, and not of Gods ſpecial grace. Secondly againſt the Proteſtantes, who on the contrarie ſide referre al to God, and take away mans freedom and proper motion in his thoughtes and doings: the Apoſtle confeſſing our good cogitations to be our owne, but not as comming of our ſelues, but of God.

notes.text: Gods grace & free will both must concurre.

annotations.title: The letter killeth.
annotations.text: ◦ As the letter of the old Law not truely vnderſtood, nor referred to Chriſt, commaunding and not giuing grace and ſpirit to fulfil that vvhich vvas commaunded, did by occaſion kill the carnal Iew: ſo the letter of the new Teſtament not truely taken nor expounded by the ſpirit of Chriſt (which is onely in his Church) killeth the ſoule of the Heretike: who alſo being carnal and void of ſpirit, gaineth nothing by the external precepts or good leſſons of the Scriptures, but rather taketh hurt by the ſame. See S. Auguſtine to. 10. Ser. 70 & 100 de tempore. & li. de Sp. & lit. c. 5. 6. & ſeq.

notes.text: The letter killeth both Iew and Heretike.

annotations.title: Much more.
annotations.text: ◦ The preeminence of the new Teſtament and of the prieſthod or Miniſterie thereof before the old, is, that the new, by al her Sacraments and Prieſts as miniſters immediate of grace and remiſsion of ſinnes, doth ſo ex opere operato giue the ſpirit of life and charitie into the hartes of the faithful, as the old did giue the letter or external act of the Lavv.

notes.text: The preeminence of the new Testament, Sacraments, &c.

annotations.title: The ſelf ſame vele.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> As the Iewes reading the old Teſtament, by reaſon of their blindnes (vvhich God for the puniſhment of their incredulitie ſuffereth to remaine as a couer vpon their eies and hartes) can not ſee Chriſt in the Scriptures which they daily heare read in their Synagogs, but ſhal, when they beleeue in him and haue the couer remoued, perceiue al to be moſt plainely done and ſpoken of him in their law & Scriptures: euen ſo Heretikes hauing (as S. Auguſtine <mn>[2]</mn> noteth) a farre greater couer of blindnes and incredulitie ouer their hartes in reſpect of the Catholike Church which they impugne, then the Iewes haue concerning Chriſt, can not ſee, though they read or heare the Scriptures read neuer ſo much, the maruelous euidence of the Catholike Church and truth in al pointes: but vvhen they ſhal returne againe to the obedience of the ſame Church, they ſhal finde the Scriptures moſt cleere for her and her doctrine, and ſhal vvonder at their former blindnes.

notes.text: The heretikes more blinde in not seing the Church, then the Iewes in not seing Christ.

annotations.title: Libertie.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> The Spirit and grace of God in the new Teſtament diſchargeth vs of the bondage of the Law and ſinne, but is not a warrant to vs of fleſhly licence, as S. Peter writeth: <mn>[2]</mn>nor diſchargeth Chriſtians of their obedience to order, law, and power of Magiſtrates ſpiritual or temporal, as ſome Heretikes of theſe daies do ſeditiouſly teach.
